blocks.text:
Over 10 days, you’ll see three very different sides of Argentina. Start in Buenos Aires with its historic neighbourhoods, Plaza de Mayo and the Casa Rosada, then spend an evening at a tango show. Next, head south to El Calafate and the Perito Moreno Glacier. Finish in subtropical Iguazú, where you can see the same waterfall system from both the Argentine and Brazilian sides.

The contrast between the regions is especially clear in this order. The capital offers architecture and city culture. Around El Calafate, you’ll find cold air, open Patagonian landscapes and ice. In Iguazú, there’s dense greenery, humid air and the constant sound of falling water.

On your free day in Buenos Aires, you can explore independently or choose an optional trip to Tigre, a ranch day with a Fiesta Gaucha, or a ferry trip to Colonia del Sacramento in Uruguay.
